refusal of therapy in patients with testicular cancer is a serious problem that is not simply related to side-effects of therapy and is not rare, and that refusal by testicular cancer pa-tients may be more common and more dangerous than previously thought.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model of patient compliance with medical advice.
the identification of the psychological and social factors that contribute to the refusal of treatment and the development of a comprehensive treatment plan for the patient who refuses.
the identification of factors that may contribute to non-compliance in testicular cancer surveillance programs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of this study do not support the use of surveillance in the treatment of patients with nonseminomatous germ cell testicular tumors.
surveillance is a viable alternative for selected patients with stage 1 non-seminomat-ous testicular cancer.
refusal of therapy in patients with cancer is not uncommon and may be related to a number of factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
patients with a high-risk disease, who refuse or are not compliant with surveillance, should be offered chemotherapy.
the majority of testicular cancer patients who are offered surveillance are compliant with follow-up.
patients who are offered surveillance for testicular cancer are a unique population and should be evaluated for the risk of non-compliance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
patients who have refused orchiectomy are at increased risk for non-compliance with surveillance and should be counseled appropriately.
patients who refuse treatment should be considered to have metastatic disease and be treated as such.
patients with non-seminoma on surveillance need to be followed very closely.
